title: Does rig's default install help Opus and Sonnet on bug-fix tasks?
question: On the same model and the same task, does Claude Code configured by rig (default config at rig main 2dbce75) pass hidden-test graders more often than Claude Code with no project config?

redactions: absolute path of the work root replaced by <work-root>
absolute path of the system temp folder replaced by <tmp>

verdict.label: claim-allowed
verdict.text: opus: ceiling (vanilla pooled 0.92 >= 0.9): uninformative, no claim. sonnet: rig helps

notes: Synthetic set A only: fixtures fx3 and fx4b, arms none (vanilla), rig and told (rig plus /craft typed first), n = 6 per cell, 72 trials. Opus ran at default effort and Sonnet at effort medium. Set B was not run.

Open flag: the sonnet vanilla arm (0/12 here) is not comparable to the sonnet none arm of 2026-11-10-rule-bug-fix-callers (15/30). Effort differs (medium here, default there) and so does the tool allowlist (node, git, ls, cat, grep and find only here).
The sonnet effect comes entirely from fx3 (vanilla 0/6, rig 6/6). On fx4b sonnet is 0/6 against 0/6, so the pooled bootstrap interval [+0.500, +0.500] is degenerate.
Descriptive only, not promotable: opus rig minus vanilla -0.333, CI [-0.500, -0.083] (fx4b: rig 1/6, vanilla 5/6).
The /craft prefix was not expanded by the harness in -p mode (craftInjected 0/72). The agent opened the hub itself in 21 of 24 told trials.
The frame path rewrite ~/.claude/ -> .claude/ differs from a real user install.
signoff.md is the orchestrator sign-off of the path rewrite, the set A only decision and the concurrency limit, recorded before the first trial.
